thread:
Marco: hey team — our private deployment started failing to decrypt model keys after a network tightening. errors from runtime: 
`rpc: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: tls: handshake failure`
and also `dial tcp: lookup kms.cust.internal: no such host`. We rolled an egress allowlist change yesterday. any quick checks?

Natasha (support): sorry about that — can you paste the minimal log around the failure and confirm whether you changed DNS/NAT/eproxy? pod id + node ip would help.

Marco: logs: 
```
2024-06-05T14:12:02Z ERROR runtime/kms: decrypt failed: tls: handshake failure
2024-06-05T14:12:02Z WARN  runtime/dialer: dial tcp: lookup kms.cust.internal on 169.254.169.253:53: no such host
2024-06-05T14:12:02Z INFO  runtime/retries: retrying decrypt (attempt 2)
```
We tightened egress to 3 external IPs and switched to forwarding DNS to an internal resolver (split-horizon). Pod: model-server-5c9f, node: ip 10.0.12.47.

Ava (support): ok first suspicion is DNS split-horizon + NAT path divergence. can you run these from the container/node: 
```
dig +short kms.cust.internal
cat /etc/resolv.conf
openssl s_client -connect kms.cust.internal:443 -servername kms.cust.internal -showcerts
curl -v --cacert /etc/redwood/ca.pem https://kms.cust.internal/health
```

Marco: results: `dig +short` from the container returns nothing (NXDOMAIN). But running `nslookup kms.cust.internal 10.2.0.2` (the internal resolver) returns `10.2.8.23`. /etc/resolv.conf in the container points at 169.254.169.253 (node agent's forwarder).

Liam (sre): that screams resolver forwarding issue — node-level resolver is pointing at metadata forwarder which doesn't have the split-horizon records. When you tightened egress did you also modify iptables or SNAT rules so DNS queries leave via a different interface? Check if kubelet's DNS stub (169.254.169.253) is reachable from the node netns. Also run `traceroute 10.2.8.23` and `tcpdump -n -i any port 53` while doing a dig to see where queries go.

Priya (infra): also note the HSM/KMS uses mTLS. If DNS is resolving intermittently to an HSM front door that expects SNI for a specific hostname, a raw IP will cause TLS handshake failures. Verify client certificate/key are mounted at `/var/lib/redwood/kms-client.{crt,key}` and that the runtime is sending the cert. If you changed the key path or alias, the KMS ACL might reject the identity — double-check the KMS subject CN vs allowed principals.

Marco: we also saw a `kms-bot` entry in logs: 
```
kms-bot: ERROR KMS-403: key access denied for /keys/customer/prod-main (principal mismatch)
```
but when we set the endpoint to the public FQDN it works (but that's not allowed for us). We definitely use an alias ARN in the config: `arn:cloudkms:region:acct:key/abcd-...` — is that incompatible with the HSM alias scheme?

Ava (support): possible mismatch. For on-prem HSM deployments our runtime expects the key identifier in the form `hsm://<cluster-id>/<key-alias>` (this is in the Private deployment README). If you supplied a cloud-KMS ARN the access path translation fails and the client may try to contact a different endpoint. Please paste your REDWOOD_KMS_ENDPOINT and REDWOOD_KEY_PATH envs.

Marco: REDWOOD_KMS_ENDPOINT=`kms.cust.internal:443`
REDWOOD_KEY_PATH=`arn:cloudkms:region:acct:key/abcd-efgh`

Liam (sre): yep that's the problem — the runtime will try to translate that ARN and hit our compatibility proxy which in your network resolves to internal HSM nodes with short-lived IPs. With DNS failing the client ends up connecting by IP (SNI mismatch) or failing to resolve -> handshake failure. Two parallel fixes: (1) fix DNS so kms.cust.internal resolves consistently from the container (ensure nodes use the internal resolver or add a pod-level stub entry); (2) update REDWOOD_KEY_PATH to the HSM native alias format or register an ARN-to-alias mapping in the Private Console.

Priya (infra): action items for infra: 
- Add egress allowlist entries for internal resolver IPs (UDP 53) and HSM cluster CIDR (TCP 443) — suggested: `10.2.0.0/16` and `10.2.8.0/24` temporarily.
- Ensure node-level resolver forwards to internal DNS (check systemd-resolved or kube-proxy config).
- Verify client certs present and readable by the runtime: `ls -l /var/lib/redwood/kms-client.*` and `openssl x509 -in /var/lib/redwood/kms-client.crt -noout -subject -issuer`.

Natasha (support): repro steps for customers/SE: 
1) replicate in staging: create a test pod in the same subnet + apply the egress allowlist as prod.
2) run the `dig`, `openssl s_client`, and `tcpdump` commands to capture DNS/TLS behavior.
3) if `dig` returns NXDOMAIN from container but not from internal resolver, add the internal resolver to pod's resolv.conf via node-level change or a kube2dns stub.
4) set `REDWOOD_KMS_DEBUG=true` and collect runtime logs.

Marco: running `tcpdump -i eth0 host 169.254.169.253` during dig shows queries leaving node and hitting a public resolver that returns NXDOMAIN. Our iptables POSTROUTING SNAT rules were forcing DNS out through the NAT gateway which doesn't have the split-horizon zone.

Liam (sre): ok that's concrete. Temporary mitigation: add a route so DNS to 10.2.0.2 goes via the internal resolver directly (no SNAT), or add iptables exception: `-p udp --dport 53 -d 10.2.0.2 -j ACCEPT` pre-SNAT. Long-term: ensure kubelet's DNS policy uses the internal resolver for that cluster/namespace.

Marco: applied the iptables exception and now `dig +short kms.cust.internal` returns `10.2.8.23`. Ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.8.23:443 -servername kms.cust.internal` and got proper cert with CN=kms.cust.internal. After restart decrypt attempts succeed. Thanks! :tada:

Natasha (support): great — can you confirm whether you want us to: (A) keep the iptables workaround and we'll shepherd infra to add a permanent rule, or (B) we'll open a Private Console ticket to map your ARN -> HSM alias and update runtime config? Also please attach the `tcpdump` and `runtime` logs to INC-2024-4927.

Marco: please do B + remove the temporary iptables tonight after mapping. we'll attach logs to the ticket.

kms-bot: NOTE: INC-2024-4927 created and assigned to eng-infra + eng-security. Links: https://redwood.internal/inc/INC-2024-4927

Ava (support): thanks everyone. summary for handoff: 
- Root cause: egress SNAT caused DNS queries to miss split-horizon internal resolver -> container resolved to no/incorrect IP -> TLS SNI mismatch and key access path translation failed.
- Short term: iptables exception to bypass SNAT for internal DNS + allowlist HSM CIDR/TCP 443.
- Long term: add ARN->HSM alias mapping in Private Console or update REDWOOD_KEY_PATH to native alias and make node DNS consistent.

Marco: confirmed working. closing from customer side once ticket created. really appreciate the quick help.
